title: Download-mode Pod is not a generation engine: hot-store OOMs it, the gen preflight kills remote mode, the watchdog is disarmed, and the stranded remote jobs paint over local truth
description:
LIVE INCIDENT, Fabio, 2026-08-11 16:01Z. He was generating locally (slow), so he opened Settings -> RunPod and connected in DOWNLOAD MODE (gpu=__cpu__) to install models onto the volume. Every model install died, the app dropped to local, and the Model Library was left showing a mix of remote and local truth on the same cards while the Pod stayed green in the RunPod console.

ONE ROOT, FOUR FAILURES. The app has no concept of 'this Pod is a download target, not a generation engine'. Remote mode is a single global flag meaning BOTH 'route generations to the Pod' AND 'route downloads to the volume'; the generation path is allowed to write the flag the download path reads; and download JOB state is not engine-scoped at all.

EVIDENCE, two clocks (app.log is UTC, RunPod console is BST, same instant):
  17:01:37 BST pod: [cubric] hot-store: staged 'loras/krea-2/style/krea2_neondrip.safetensors' (469291992 bytes)
  17:01:39 BST pod: start-cpu.sh: line 69: 21 Killed  python -m uvicorn wrapper:app --port 8889
  17:01:44 BST pod: WARN: container is unhealthy: exit code 137: triggered memory limits (OOM)
  16:01:39Z app: hot-store ensure HTTP 502 - generating from volume
  16:01:39Z app: remote install SSE closed; 4 dep(s) outstanding - recovering
  16:01:41Z app: Remote mode disabled
  16:01:41Z app: Remote engine not connected - falling back to the local engine.
The CPU Pod has 3.725 GiB RAM (telemetry). It was healthy and serving /health 200 OK two seconds before the stage. Hot-store OOM-killed the wrapper. The Pod then RESTARTED ITSELF (17:01:44 'start container: begin') and healed; the app never came back because it had already flipped remote mode off.

FAILURE 1 - HOT-STORE RUNS ON A CPU POD (the cause). Half-wire between twins in js/services/commandExecutor.js: the stage-on-CONNECT prefetch at :570 guards cfg.gpuType === '__cpu__', the per-GEN preflight call at :1505 does not. Then :463 makes it lethal - _remoteVramGb returns null for __cpu__, and null is read at :497 as 'unknown -> no VRAM cap', so on the LEAST capable box the size filter is at its MOST permissive: stage every dep >=100MB with no ceiling. A download-mode Pod must never stage anything; the user is not generating there.

FAILURE 2 - THE GEN PREFLIGHT TEARS DOWN REMOTE MODE (the blast radius). js/services/comfyController.js :637-646 reads /remote/comfy/status, sees not-ready, and falls through to a teardown that POSTs /remote/mode {active:false}. noGpu appears NOWHERE in comfyController.js even though the status route already returns it (routes/remotePodLifecycle.js:646). A download-mode Pod is never 'ready' for generation BY DESIGN, so any generation attempt while download mode is active tears down remote mode. The existing MPI-275 guard (if check.connecting) is the same class of fix with a hole in it - do not add a fourth guard clause without closing the concept.

FAILURE 3 - THE WATCHDOG IS DISARMED, THEN ABANDONS SILENTLY. Both recovery paths in routes/downloadManager.js bail on !remoteModels.isRemoteActive(): the SSE-close reconnect at :1936 ('Pod gone - nothing to recover to') and the stall watchdog armed at :1894. Failure 2 flipped that flag one second after the SSE closed, so the scheduled reconnect fired into a disarmed guard and returned. That half is collateral and dies with failure 2. THE INDEPENDENT HALF DOES NOT: even on a legitimate disconnect the outstanding deps stay in _depJobs as 'downloading' forever, with no failure surfaced and no user-visible signal. Abandonment must fail the jobs and say so. Compare memory tool_watcher_that_can_never_fire.

FAILURE 4 - STRANDED REMOTE JOBS PAINT OVER LOCAL TRUTH. Fabio: 'The UI is showing a mix of being connected to the pod and being local at the same time.' Observed: MiniMax H3 Reference renders '/ INSTALLED' AND an 8% progress bar at once, and Boogu Image Edit sits at 'Queued...' - both remote-queued, both rendered while the app is local. Mechanism: the disconnect edge at js/shell.js:1554 re-checks INSTALLED state against the local filesystem (correct, MPI-85), but nothing touches download JOB state. _depJobs (routes/downloadManager.js:555) is ONE unscoped depId -> DepJob map and its ONLY clear site is cancel-all at :3075. GET /comfy/downloads/status (:1515) serves that map verbatim, so a stranded remote job's percentage survives the disconnect and overpaints the freshly-corrected local installed-state on the same card.

SCOPE. Fix 1 stops the OOM. Fix 2 stops any future disconnect from killing in-flight downloads. Fix 3 makes silent abandonment impossible. Fix 4 makes the Model Library show one engine's truth at a time. Fabio asked for 1, 2 and 3 by name and reported 4 directly.

NOT IN SCOPE, CARD SEPARATELY: the stale OS notification ('Generation complete - 2 generations finished' fired ~1h late, on the landing page, for work already done). js/shell/notificationService.js:32 _doneCount is a module-level counter that only flushes when generationQueueCount reaches 0 and nothing expires it, so a batch counted at 16:05 fires whenever the count next reaches 0. Same session, different subsystem.
